en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 22.5.
Kusala-ttika, Cūḷantara-duka.

A non-wholesome, non-non-conditioned state is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a wholesome, conditioned state. ... [There are] six in the case of the object, and six in the cases of predominance (*adhipati*) and decisive support (*upanissaya*).

(The conditioned is the same as the "with-conditions" [section]. In dependence on a non-wholesome, non-visible state, a neutral, visible state arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated. There are six in the case of the root, six in the case of predominance ... pe ... three in the case of result (*vipāka*) ... pe ... six in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*).
An unwholesome and non-manifesting state is related to a wholesome and non-manifesting state by way of object-condition.

(Nine questions are to be formulated. There are nine [answers] for the object-condition, three for the predominance-condition, and nine each for the decisive-support, prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions.
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor impinging, an indeterminate impinging state arises by way of the root condition.
(Abbreviated. Six for root, six for predominance … pe … three for mutuality … pe … three for result … pe … six for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor non-impinging, an indeterminate non-impinging state arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Three for root, three for predominance … pe … three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a non-wholesome non-material phenomenon, a neutral material phenomenon arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Six in the case of the root condition, six in the case of the predominance condition … pe … three in the case of the mutuality condition … pe … three in the case of the resultant condition … pe … six in the case of the non-disappearance condition.

Dependent on a non-wholesome non-material phenomenon, a neutral immaterial phenomenon arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Three in the case of the root condition … pe … three in the case of the non-disappearance condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor mundane, a neutral mundane state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Five under root; five under predominance … pe … three under result … pe … five under non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor supramundane, a wholesome supramundane state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor supramundane, a neutral supramundane state arises by way of root condition.

(Six questions are to be formulated. Under root condition there are six; under predominance condition there are six … pe … under result condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are six.
In dependence on a state that is neither wholesome nor cognizable by any [consciousness], a state that is unwholesome and cognizable by some [consciousness] arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root condition there are eighteen; under object condition there are nine … pe … under result condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are eighteen.
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor cognizable by anyone, there arises an unwholesome state cognizable by someone, by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. [In the root condition there are] eighteen; in the object condition, nine ... pe ... in the resultant condition, three ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, eighteen.
